page: Hetzner Cloud ccx53 is a general purpose cloud server offering dedicated compute resources based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor line. Virtualized via QEMU, the instance is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include standard AVX, AES, and SHA-NI for cryptographic operations, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent.

System memory consists of 125.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of approximately 3.91 GB per core. The server includes 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates without bundled hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic testing highlights strong memory throughput, reflected by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 2995.56 and 103.84 GB/s uncached read bandwidth. Cryptographic operations also place in the upper quartile with a PassMark encryption score of 38690.08, aided by native AES instruction support.

Compute benchmarks indicate consistent mid-tier execution across larger workloads, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 12028.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 47702.95. Single-core stress-ng tests place in the top 25 percent at 3046.68, while lightweight LLM text generation reaches 353.73 tokens per second on small parameter sets. Across large-scale operations, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 195.41 GB/s and Redis yields 42.08 million set operations per second.

By delivering fully dedicated cores and fast local NVMe storage without shared-tenant CPU contention, the ccx53 instance balances raw processing and memory footprint. It is well matched for sustained relational databases, intermediate caching layers, build pipelines, enterprise backend applications, and static web serving workloads requiring predictable dedicated CPU execution.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx53 is a general purpose server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz, 125.0 GB of system memory, and 600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. The hardware incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache along with AES and SHA-NI cryptographic instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions. In benchmark evaluations, the ccx53 demonstrates top-decile PassMark memory performance and upper-quartile encryption results, alongside reliable mid-range multi-core CPU throughput across Geekbench and PassMark suites. The 1:4 core-to-memory configuration and dedicated CPU allocation make the ccx53 suited for production relational database hosting, continuous integration pipelines, caching services, and multi-threaded enterprise web applications requiring predictable compute consistency.
